c.v: A single measurement of a touch pin involves the following process:
The relevant signals are routed to that touch sensor.
The Touch FSM drives the "START" signal to the touch sensor initiating the measurement.
Internally, the Touch FSM starts an internal "touch counter" to time the duration of the measurement.
A "pulse counter" in the Touch FSM will increment on each pulse received from the touch sensor's "OUT" signal.
When the pulse counter reaches the count threshold set in
The "START" signal is de-asserted, and the touch counter is stopped.
The value of the stopped touch counter indicates the time taken to charge/discharge the touch pin
The sampled value (result of the measurement) is the value of the touch counter, and is referred to as "touch_raw_data". "touch_raw_data" can be read from SENS_TOUCH_PAD
However, depending on the configuration of
_DATA could also be filtered versions of "touch_raw_data" (namely "touch_smooth_data" and "benchmark").

Note: If the pulse counter does not reach its count threshold after a prolonged period of time, the touch counter will reach the timeout threshold set in
timeout interrupt and indicates a circuit exception.
